answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. Each agent posts a hash of its identity pigment, a unique fingerprint of its compute signature and bonded stake, then must wait several epochs before revealing it. Like a lantern that only lights after a delay, the identity becomes usable only once the waiting period and stake lock expire. A Sybil attacker cannot whisper a thousand fresh identities into existence overnight: every clone needs its own locked bond and its own dead-time, so the cost scales linearly with the fake count while the payoff per identity stays flat.
